newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Argentine Cavallo says dollar peg best for LatAm.
newsitem.headline: Argentine Cavallo says dollar peg best for LatAm.

text.p: Former Argentine economy minister Domingo Cavallo reaffirmed in an interview with Brazil's Istoe magazine that fixed exchange rates were the best option for Latin American economies.
Asked whether parity with the dollar was the only way out for Latin economies, he answered: "Yes."

"In Mexico there is now a discussion going on whether to adopt the Argentine model," Cavallo told Istoe. "This would eliminate uncertainties in monetary policy and allow the country to lower interest rates and experience more vigorous economic growth."

He said there was no risk that Argentina or Brazil could face the same problems as Mexico because both countries had lower current account deficits and were working hard to promote internal development.

Cavallo, who plans to run in the 1999 presidential elections, said he would continue with the reforms implemented while he was economy minister, adding that a fixed exchange rate would continue to be the best policy for Argentina for many years to come.
"For a long time, I would say for decades, it won't be possible to speculate with exchange rates here (Argentina)," he said.
Cavallo, who resigned as economy minister last year, said he was confident he could garner enough popular support to make a successful bid for the presidency.

"I am much more popular than those people who remained in government," he said. "I feel that my strength comes from those people who want a change in social policy and above all an improved justice system."
Cavallo said current Argentine President Carlos Menem did not have the political will or the courage to fight against organized crime and corruption.

He said the next Argentine government would take the shape of a coalition of parties grouping around one candidate, and that the political movement he was launching would provide a key ingredient to build this coalition of forces.
((-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
